items.followUp: What is the difference between volatile and non-volatile memory?

rubric.why: Retaining data when power is off is the defining property of non-volatile memory.
rubric.description: States that non-volatile memory retains data without power.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for this defining property.

rubric.why: A valid example shows understanding of non-volatile memory.
rubric.description: Gives at least one valid example.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for one or more valid examples.

modelAnswer: Non-volatile memory retains its data even when the computer’s power is switched off.
Examples include ROM and flash memory.

items.followUp: Draw the truth table for P OR Q OR NOT Q.

rubric.why: NOT P must be the complement of P for every input pair.
rubric.description: Gives the correct NOT P values for all four input rows.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the complete, correct NOT P column.

rubric.why: P OR Q OR NOT P is true for all four input pairs.
rubric.description: Gives the correct final result for all four rows.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the complete, correct final column.

modelAnswer: Here, + means OR, and NOT P is the complement of P.
| P | Q | NOT P | P + Q + NOT(P) |

items.followUp: What is the main difference between a hub and a switch?

rubric.why: Connecting computers or other devices on a network is the shared function of hubs and switches.
rubric.description: States that a hub or switch connects computers or devices on a network.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the shared network-connection function.

rubric.why: A correct description of how either device handles data adds a distinguishing detail.
rubric.description: States that a hub broadcasts data to all ports or that a switch forwards data to its destination.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct description of either device’s data handling.

modelAnswer: A hub or switch is a networking device used to connect computers or other devices in a LAN.
A hub sends received data to all its ports, whereas a switch forwards data to the intended device.
